replacements.text: Strongest feature: Craig presents an auditable eliminative inference: if law, chance, and design exhaust fine-tuning’s explanations, excluding the first two makes design follow, connecting conditions to God’s existence. Principal limitation: The excerpt neither demonstrates the trilemma’s exhaustiveness nor supplies evidence eliminating law and chance, and offers no likelihood or predictive specificity showing that design explains observations better. Live burden: Craig must defend the option set, articulate a principled probability model, and derive distinctive designer expectations, while Flew must identify a credible rival explanation rather than rest solely on skepticism. Locked score: The exact 69 reflects logical coherence 58, evidence warrant 52, responsiveness 88, relevance and burden 82, precision and clarity 88, and calibration and charity 57: excellent directness cannot overcome unsupported eliminations and categorical overstatement.

Strongest feature: Flew directly challenges Craig’s chance-elimination premise: without cosmic propensities or a frequency class of other universes, probability interpretations cannot ground claims of astronomically unlikely fine-tuning. Principal limitation: Showing that propensity and frequency interpretations lack inputs does not establish every epistemic, Bayesian, or model-relative assignment as illegitimate, nor answer qualitative comparison based on relative surprise. Live burden: Flew must demonstrate why no principled measure sustains Craig’s comparison, while Craig must specify his measure, justify its assumptions, and show the design inference remains robust across reasonable alternatives. Locked score: The exact 81 reflects logical coherence 80, evidence warrant 73, responsiveness 88, relevance and burden 85, precision and clarity 85, and calibration and charity 80: a consequential objection remains limited by unexamined probabilistic frameworks.
